hypothesis: Wave D13 (C_L3_OPENNESS_ORDER): openness K sets a ceiling on the work a system draws between T_h and T_c, reached at eta_CA = 1 - sqrt(T_c/T_h). AI reading tested here: systems that keep order from their openness run near that ceiling, so real thermal power plants show eta_obs close to eta_CA.

observable.quantity: m = median over plants of |eta_obs / eta_CA - 1|
observable.domain: thermal power plants (nuclear, coal, steam, gas turbine) listed with T_h, T_c and eta_obs in Esposito et al. (2010) PRL 105, 150603 (arXiv:1008.2464)

prediction_method.description: T_h, T_c and eta_obs of every plant in the table transcribed after approval from the arXiv source as published; eta_CA computed from T_h and T_c; the table's own derived columns (eta_C, eta_-, eta_+) not used. The script refuses to run unless this card is APPROVED and the data sha256 matches.

fixed_parameters: all plants in the table, none removed
median of |eta_obs/eta_CA - 1| (robust to one odd plant; AI choice)
fail_criterion: FAILED if the median |eta_obs/eta_CA - 1| >= 0.25. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise or with fewer than 8 plants.
note: Disclosure: to find the table the drafter read the paper's abstract and, with every digit masked, the table's caption, column heads and plant names; no temperature or efficiency was seen. The paper's text says the Curzon-Ahlborn efficiency describes actual plants very well (seen while locating the table), and the drafter recalls that from the literature; a PASS is plausible, but the median could land anywhere and gas turbines are known to differ. T_h, T_c are as reported (steam or combustion temperatures, cooling water), not the true reservoirs; plants are designed for cost, not only power. The step from D13's ceiling to 'real systems run near it' is an AI interpretation; a FAILED would remove that reading, not the D13 ceiling. Nearest theory: Curzon-Ahlborn, Novikov, low-dissipation engines. Not UET-distinct. Approved by the author in chat on 2026-11-25 as drafted ("Approve and run"); this approval is committed before the table's numbers are read.
